# What the market evidence can and cannot yet say (RQ3 and H6) {#sec-markets}

The title of this section was fixed before any post-seal industry return was read by code, by the pre-registered plausibility rule D11 (@sec-methods; @sec-app-pap), which compares the minimum detectable effect (MDE) of the primary H5 test with a threshold of {{< var design.plausibility_pp >}} pp of annualised alpha per SD of exposure. At {{< var power.power_pct >}}% power and Holm's first-step level of {{< var design.alpha.h5_first >}}, the primary MDE is {{< var d11.primary_mde >}} pp per SD. It exceeds the threshold, so the rule fires: RQ3 is reported under this title, and the paper is led by RQ1 and RQ2 (@sec-rq1, @sec-rq2). The threshold was written into the plan before the power analysis first ran but became binding only when confirmed with the MDE in view (PAP §7). The MDE is printed beside every confirmatory market null below; no MDE is computed for the exploratory ones.

## The confirmatory test of H5 and H5b

@tbl-rq3-confirmatory reproduces the record of the single confirmatory run (@sec-methods), which used all {{< var rq3.provenance.n >}} FF49 industries (dropped for a missing return: {{< var rq3.provenance.dropped >}}) and {{< var rq3.provenance.n_days >}} factor days from {{< var design.window.start >}} to {{< var design.window.end >}}. The primary null is D21's b = b̄ and the statistic (b̂ − b̄)/s (@sec-methods). For H5, b̂ = {{< var rq3.h5.b >}} pp per SD against b̄ = {{< var rq3.h5.bbar >}} and s = {{< var rq3.h5.s >}}, so T = {{< var rq3.h5.t >}} and p = {{< var rq3.h5.p >}}. For H5b, which holds the AIOE benchmark [@felten2021occupational] in the regression, b̂ = {{< var rq3.h5b.b >}} against b̄ = {{< var rq3.h5b.bbar >}} and s = {{< var rq3.h5b.s >}}, so T = {{< var rq3.h5b.t >}} and p = {{< var rq3.h5b.p >}}. Neither p reaches the first-step level, so Holm's procedure [@holm1979simple] stops there: H5 is {{< var rq3.h5.decision_text >}}, and H5b is {{< var rq3.h5b.decision_text >}}.

Every number in @tbl-rq3-confirmatory carries the S1 timing caveat (PAP §10): Design B is out of sample in its AEI data only, not strictly real-time. Its OEWS {{< var vintage.oews.primary >}} weights were released on {{< var design.s1.oews_release >}}, after the formation date of {{< var design.formation >}} and inside the return window, and its O\*NET {{< var vintage.onet.primary >}} task links also postdate formation, although their task text is byte-identical to that of O\*NET {{< var vintage.onet.r32 >}} (PAP §11, C-74). R32, the strict real-time row on the OEWS {{< var vintage.oews.r32 >}} weights public at formation, gives b̂ = {{< var rob.r32.h5.estimate >}} for H5 (interval [{{< var rob.r32.h5.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r32.h5.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r32.h5.p >}}) and {{< var rob.r32.h5b.estimate >}} for H5b ([{{< var rob.r32.h5b.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rob.r32.h5b.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rob.r32.h5b.p >}}). R1, on the later OEWS {{< var vintage.oews.r1 >}} weights, is look-ahead: {{< var rob.r01.h5.estimate >}} for H5 and {{< var rob.r01.h5b.estimate >}} for H5b (@sec-robustness).

The co-primary specifications share the run and the table. R12 replaces exposure by its standardised ranks. R13 drops Softw, the industry with the largest Design B `z_delegation` ({{< var audit.exposure.b.z_del_max >}} SD). Under R12 both slopes are negative: {{< var rq3.h5_r12.b >}} for H5 (T = {{< var rq3.h5_r12.t_bbar >}}, p = {{< var rq3.h5_r12.p_primary >}}) and {{< var rq3.h5b_r12.b >}} for H5b (T = {{< var rq3.h5b_r12.t_bbar >}}, p = {{< var rq3.h5b_r12.p_primary >}}). Under R13 they are {{< var rq3.h5_r13.b >}} (T = {{< var rq3.h5_r13.t_bbar >}}, p = {{< var rq3.h5_r13.p_primary >}}) and {{< var rq3.h5b_r13.b >}} (T = {{< var rq3.h5b_r13.t_bbar >}}, p = {{< var rq3.h5b_r13.p_primary >}}), each on its own, larger scale (s = {{< var rq3.h5_r13.s >}} and {{< var rq3.h5b_r13.s >}}). The claim that delegation exposure is priced in this window beyond the historical pattern required a primary rejection together with an R13 rejection at the same Holm level. No primary is rejected, so the co-condition is not met for either hypothesis.

## The fixed wording

The script's P14 wording of each non-rejection (PAP §3.3), verbatim from the record behind @tbl-rq3-confirmatory, with the S1 caveat above (R32):

> {{< var rq3.h5.wording >}}

> {{< var rq3.h5b.wording >}}

The paper does not paraphrase these sentences into a statement that the market did not price delegation. Their null is narrower than the approved hypothesis (@sec-methods): a rejection would have said that the slope departs from what this exposure vector showed over {{< var design.null_years >}}, not that it differs from zero.

## Intervals, the R13 MDE and the secondary null

Two intervals are reported for each hypothesis, b̂ ± c·s at each Holm level. For H5 they are [{{< var rq3.h5.ci_005.lo_pp2 >}}, {{< var rq3.h5.ci_005.hi_pp2 >}}] pp per SD at {{< var design.alpha.h5_second >}} and [{{< var rq3.h5.ci_0025.lo_pp2 >}}, {{< var rq3.h5.ci_0025.hi_pp2 >}}] at {{< var design.alpha.h5_first >}}. For H5b they are [{{< var rq3.h5b.ci_005.lo_pp2 >}}, {{< var rq3.h5b.ci_005.hi_pp2 >}}] and [{{< var rq3.h5b.ci_0025.lo_pp2 >}}, {{< var rq3.h5b.ci_0025.hi_pp2 >}}]. The co-conditioned claim has R13's larger MDE at the first-step level, {{< var rq3.h5.mde_r13 >}} pp for H5 and {{< var rq3.h5b.mde_r13 >}} pp for H5b, so a pricing claim robust to dropping Softw had {{< var power.power_pct >}}% power only near those values (@tbl-rq3-confirmatory).

The zero-slope statistic from the same run is a secondary null, not part of the decision: T = {{< var rq3.h5.b0.t >}} and p = {{< var rq3.h5.b0.p >}} for H5, beside an MDE of {{< var rq3.h5.mde >}} pp per SD (the primary's s and first-step critical), and T = {{< var rq3.h5b.b0.t >}} and p = {{< var rq3.h5b.b0.p >}} for H5b, beside an MDE of {{< var rq3.h5b.mde >}} pp. Both carry the S1 caveat (R32).

The robustness rows that move b̂ most are R7 (dropping Hardw, Softw and Chips), R12 (ranks) and R5 (equal-weighted returns) for H5, and R12, R7 and R6 (FF30) for H5b; their values are in @sec-robustness and @sec-app-robustness-tables. Each carries the S1 caveat and none changes a decision (PAP §8.1).

## Secondary inference

Randomisation inference, oversized on the pre-seal windows (@sec-methods), is kept as secondary, each p printed with its documented size at a nominal {{< var design.alpha.h5_first >}}. With {{< var rq3.secondary.n_permutations >}} permutations each, permuting `z_delegation` gives p = {{< var rq3.secondary.ri_h5 >}} for H5 (size {{< var rq3.secondary.size_pct.ri_h5 >}}%), and permuting it with `z_aioe` held in place gives p = {{< var rq3.secondary.ri_h5b >}} for H5b (size {{< var rq3.secondary.size_pct.ri_h5b >}}%, oversized even under exchangeability). The Freedman–Lane scheme [@freedman1983nonstochastic; @winkler2014permutation] gives p = {{< var rq3.secondary.fl_h5b >}} for H5b scored by the pivotal t (size {{< var rq3.secondary.size_pct.fl_pivotal_h5b >}}%) and {{< var rq3.secondary.fl_coef_h5b >}} scored by the coefficient (size {{< var rq3.secondary.size_pct.fl_coef_h5b >}}%). Conventional OLS with HC3 standard errors gives, for reference, {{< var rq3.secondary.hc3_h5_b >}} (SE {{< var rq3.secondary.hc3_h5_se >}}) for H5 and {{< var rq3.secondary.hc3_h5b_b >}} (SE {{< var rq3.secondary.hc3_h5b_se >}}) for H5b. None of these enters the decision.

## The influence of Softw

@tbl-rq3-influence-softw (@sec-app-supplementary) reports Softw's influence on the confirmatory fits, post-result diagnostics that PAP §3.3 (P11) places outside the decision. Softw's leverage is {{< var rq3.influence.softw.h5.leverage >}} in the H5 fit and {{< var rq3.influence.softw.h5b.leverage >}} in the H5b fit. Its DFBETAS on b are {{< var rq3.influence.softw.h5.dfbetas >}} and {{< var rq3.influence.softw.h5b.dfbetas >}}, and its Cook's distances are {{< var rq3.influence.softw.h5.cooks_d >}} and {{< var rq3.influence.softw.h5b.cooks_d >}}. The industries with the largest Cook's distance in each fit, listed in @tbl-rq3-influence-top, are Gold and Hardw, not Softw. This agrees with the R13 estimates lying close to the primaries.

## Exploratory market analyses

Exploratory: Design A reads returns from the market seal, {{< var design.seal_date >}}, to {{< var design.window.end >}} (PAP §8.3, D19). `A_r2` uses release r2 alone and is numerically identical to Design B, so the Design B rows below are the `A_r2` rows over a sub-window, not independent evidence. `A_pooled`, which is look-ahead, pools releases r2 to r6, of which r3 to r6 were published during and after the return window (PAP §10); its largest `z_delegation`, again {{< var audit.exposure.a_pooled.z_del_max_industry >}}, is {{< var audit.exposure.a_pooled.z_del_max >}} SD. Design A is exploratory because general knowledge of post-seal market moves cannot be removed (PAP §0.4); nothing here tests H5 or H5b or carries error control.

Exploratory: the event studies use the D19 rule. The events are ChatGPT, which the design specification names, and every flagship model announcement by OpenAI, Anthropic or Google's AI labs in a named source over the period the rule fixes (@tbl-rq3-event-dates; @sec-app-supplementary). Day zero is the first trading day on or after the announcement; @tbl-rq3-event-days lists moved dates and overlapping windows. The rule's exceptions (excluding Gemma and Gemini Ultra, adding ChatGPT by name, accepting an OpenAI release's absence from the source) were chosen with the source's list, and so the dates, in view (PAP §0.4). Each industry's cumulative abnormal return (CAR) over an FF5+UMD fit [@fama2015five; @carhart1997persistence] is regressed across industries on exposure, with HC3 standard errors.

Exploratory: @tbl-rq3-event-slopes and @fig-rq3-event-slopes (@sec-app-supplementary) report every event, horizon and design. For ChatGPT, the `A_r2` slope is {{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k5.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.b >}} pp of CAR per SD at the shorter horizon (CI [{{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k5.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k5.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.ci_hi >}}], nominal p = {{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k5.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.p >}}) and {{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k20.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.b >}} at the longer one ([{{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k20.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k20.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.ci_hi >}}], nominal p = {{< var rq3.event.chatgpt.k20.a_r2.z_delegation.z_delegation.p >}}). The p-values are nominal and single-test, and may be oversized because abnormal returns are correlated across industries on a common date.

Exploratory: the tercile portfolios go long the highest-exposure third of FF49 industries and short the lowest, with membership fixed at formation, monthly capitalisation weights and equal-weighted legs beside them (PAP §8.3, D19). They report CAPM, FF3 and FF5+UMD alphas [@fama1993common] with Newey–West errors [@newey1987simple; @newey1994automatic], stationary-bootstrap intervals [@politis1994stationary], and the probabilistic (PSR) and deflated (DSR) Sharpe ratios [@bailey2012sharpe; @bailey2014deflated]. They are measurement devices that express the cross-sectional slope as a return spread, not strategies; the costed versions show the spread's fragility, not a tradable return (@tbl-rq3-terciles-b-cap-costs; @sec-app-supplementary).

Exploratory: for Design B (secondary) with cap-weighted legs, the annualised mean high-minus-low return is {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.mean.estimate >}} pp (bootstrap CI [{{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.mean.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.mean.ci_hi >}}], nominal p = {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.mean.p >}}). The FF3 alpha is {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.alpha_ff3.estimate >}} pp and the FF5+UMD alpha {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.alpha_ff5_umd.estimate >}} pp ([{{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.alpha_ff5_umd.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.alpha_ff5_umd.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.alpha_ff5_umd.p >}}). That spread across factor models rests on {{< var design.window.months >}} monthly returns and is model-fragile (@tbl-rq3-terciles-b-cap; @sec-app-supplementary). The PSR is {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.psr.estimate >}} and the DSR {{< var rq3.terciles.b.cap.dsr.estimate >}}; with equal-weighted legs they are {{< var rq3.terciles.b.ew.psr.estimate >}} and {{< var rq3.terciles.b.ew.dsr.estimate >}}. @tbl-rq3-terciles-dsr gives them for `A_r2` and for `A_pooled` (look-ahead). The DSR treats every variant as an independent trial, which overstates the number of independent trials: B is nested in `A_r2`, and `A_r2` and `A_pooled` hold nearly the same portfolios (@fig-rq3-tercile-cumulative).

Exploratory: Fama–MacBeth regressions [@fama1973risk] of monthly industry excess returns on exposure, log size, log book-to-market and momentum give a mean exposure slope of {{< var rq3.fama_macbeth.b.z.mean >}} pp per month per SD for Design B over {{< var rq3.fama_macbeth.b.z.n_months >}} months (CI [{{< var rq3.fama_macbeth.b.z.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rq3.fama_macbeth.b.z.ci_hi >}}], nominal p = {{< var rq3.fama_macbeth.b.z.p >}}; @tbl-rq3-fama-macbeth-b; @sec-app-supplementary). For `A_r2` over {{< var rq3.fama_macbeth.a_r2.z.n_months >}} months it is {{< var rq3.fama_macbeth.a_r2.z.mean >}} ([{{< var rq3.fama_macbeth.a_r2.z.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rq3.fama_macbeth.a_r2.z.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rq3.fama_macbeth.a_r2.z.p >}}; @tbl-rq3-fama-macbeth-a-r2). For `A_pooled`, look-ahead, it is {{< var rq3.fama_macbeth.a_pooled.z.mean >}} ([{{< var rq3.fama_macbeth.a_pooled.z.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rq3.fama_macbeth.a_pooled.z.ci_hi >}}], p = {{< var rq3.fama_macbeth.a_pooled.z.p >}}; @tbl-rq3-fama-macbeth-a-pooled).

Exploratory: the comparison with Eisfeldt, Schubert and Zhang [@eisfeldt2023generative], who report higher returns for more exposed firms, asks only for the sign of the CAR slope on `z_aioe` around the ChatGPT release, before `z_delegation` is added. At the FF49 level, which is not their firm-level design, the slope in the first step is {{< var rq3.eisfeldt.step1.b >}} pp of CAR per SD of `z_aioe` (CI [{{< var rq3.eisfeldt.step1.ci_lo >}}, {{< var rq3.eisfeldt.step1.ci_hi >}}], nominal p = {{< var rq3.eisfeldt.step1.p >}}; @tbl-rq3-eisfeldt-step1; @sec-app-supplementary). The sign is negative and the interval contains zero, so their sign is not reproduced at this level of aggregation. @tbl-rq3-eisfeldt-step2 adds `z_delegation` for `A_r2` and for `A_pooled` (look-ahead).

## Talk versus use (H6, exploratory)

Exploratory: H6 (PAP §6, D18) belongs to no testing family. For the gap, the talk index T (@sec-methods) uses filings dated {{< var h6.talk.filed_start >}} to {{< var h6.talk.filed_end >}}, public before formation. Pooled across all filers, the share rises from {{< var h6.talk.pooled_all.y2019 >}} in the first filing year to {{< var h6.talk.pooled_all.y2024 >}} in {{< var h6.talk.year >}} and {{< var h6.talk.pooled_all.y2025 >}} in the last (@tbl-h6-talk-by-year, @fig-h6-talk-by-year). Over the same years the share of filers with no FF49 industry rises from {{< var h6.talk.unmapped_share_pct.y2019 >}}% to {{< var h6.talk.unmapped_share_pct.y2025 >}}%, so part of that trend is composition; the mapped-only series runs from {{< var h6.talk.pooled_mapped.y2019 >}} to {{< var h6.talk.pooled_mapped.y2025 >}}.

Exploratory: across industries, the Spearman correlation of T with Design B `z_usage` (conversations matched to O\*NET tasks) is {{< var h6.spearman.rho >}}, industry-bootstrap CI [{{< var h6.spearman.ci.lo >}}, {{< var h6.spearman.ci.hi >}}] (@tbl-h6-divergence, @fig-h6-talk-vs-usage). Its p (t-approximation, n minus two degrees of freedom) is {{< var diag.h6.none.p >}}, nominal and exploratory (PAP §11 D-3; @sec-app-deviations), a post-result diagnostic in no testing family. Two inputs are fixed at retrieval, not in {{< var h6.talk.year >}}: each filer's industry is its current SIC from the EDGAR submissions file, retrieved at {{< var h6.vintage.submissions_retrieved_utc >}} and applied to every filing year (PAP §11, C-40), and the numerator uses the SEC's phrase matching as implemented on the retrieval date (PAP §6).

{{< include _generated/figures/h6-talk-vs-usage.md >}}

Exploratory: the leave-one-industry-out Spearman in @tbl-diag-h6-influence is a post-result diagnostic (PAP §11 D-3); exploratory; not a decision. Leaving out Softw gives {{< var diag.h6.softw.rho >}} ([{{< var diag.h6.softw.ci_lo >}}, {{< var diag.h6.softw.ci_hi >}}]); leaving out Hardw, {{< var diag.h6.hardw.rho >}} ([{{< var diag.h6.hardw.ci_lo >}}, {{< var diag.h6.hardw.ci_hi >}}]), and BusSv, {{< var diag.h6.bussv.rho >}} ([{{< var diag.h6.bussv.ci_lo >}}, {{< var diag.h6.bussv.ci_hi >}}]), give intervals crossing zero; every leave-out is in the table. The R29 parts whose intervals also cover zero are the change from the first filing year, float weighting and the pre-formation filings (@sec-robustness).

Exploratory: the gap (@tbl-h6-gap-ranking) in place of `z_delegation`, under recomputed historical-null inference (@sec-methods; @tbl-h6-gap-returns), gives b̂ = {{< var h6.gap_returns.b >}} pp of annualised alpha per SD of gap (interval [{{< var h6.gap_returns.ci.lo >}}, {{< var h6.gap_returns.ci.hi >}}]; T = {{< var h6.gap_returns.t_bbar >}}, nominal p = {{< var h6.gap_returns.p_bbar >}} against b = b̄; against the secondary null of a zero slope, T = {{< var h6.gap_returns.t_zero >}}, nominal p = {{< var h6.gap_returns.p_zero >}}); no MDE computed (exploratory); in no testing family; Design B's S1 caveat applies.

## What a future window would need

The MDE is {{< var power.mde_over_s >}} × s, with s the spread of the historical slope across {{< var design.window.months >}}-month windows ({{< var power.s.h5 >}} for H5, {{< var power.s.h5b >}} for H5b; @sec-methods); for the H5 MDE to reach the {{< var design.plausibility_pp >}} pp threshold, a window's s would have to fall to that threshold divided by {{< var power.mde_over_s >}}, and a claim robust to dropping Softw would need the same of R13's scale (MDEs {{< var rq3.h5.mde_r13 >}} and {{< var rq3.h5b.mde_r13 >}} pp). What the evidence cannot yet say is whether this exposure vector is priced by a departure smaller than {{< var rq3.h5.mde >}} and {{< var rq3.h5b.mde >}} pp per SD (@tbl-rq3-confirmatory).
